title: S-Boxes Preserving Algebraic Degree Across Rounds
summary: The results rely on key addition and exclude permutations; identifying S-box families that preserve algebraic degree through more keyed rounds remains open.

formal_statement.body: For key-alternating block ciphers, determine which individual S-boxes or families of S-boxes permit the algebraic degree of the block cipher to be preserved when additional keyed rounds are appended.

scope.domain: Algebraic-degree analysis of S-box-based key-alternating block ciphers.
parameters: S-box or S-box family: nonlinear component to be characterized
Additional keyed rounds: extension depth over which algebraic-degree preservation is sought
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the individual S-boxes or S-box families that preserve the block cipher's algebraic degree when additional keyed rounds are appended.

citations.label: Strong and Tight Security Guarantees against Integral Distinguishers

progress.summary: The paper presents this question in its conclusion as a future direction for extending algebraic-degree reasoning to more rounds. It calls for a better understanding of which S-boxes or S-box families enable degree preservation.
citation_labels: Phil Hebborn et al., Strong and Tight Security Guarantees against Integral Distinguishers
